texts: Swap to match 3 or more tiles in a row.

Get rid of the tiles under this piece to 
eject it from the bottom of the playing 
field. It will then appear in the item 
outline to the left.

Eject all items from the bottom of the 
playing field to complete each level.

Match four or more tiles to recharge the 
magic pot and clear the way for items. The 
magic pot must be charged to 100% to use 
it.
Complete the level before the lamp's oil burns out.

This tile is locked. Pair it with matching 
tiles to break the lock.

The Bomb of Sinbad the Sailor gets rid 
of clusters of tiles on the game field. 
Click the bomb and then point to the 
tiles you want to smash.

The Hourglass of King Shehriyar adds 
30 seconds to the timer by clicking it.

Match three or more tiles to reveal the 
picture hidden behind the game field.

The Lightning of Malice eliminates one 
kind of gem from the entire game area. 
Click on the lightning and then the gem 
you want to smash.

Eject this pack of bonus points from 
the bottom of the playing field to boost 
your score.

A double-locked tile. Remember what 
to do?

The Silver Moon of Queen Zumurrud swaps 
two tiles that couldn't otherwise be 
swapped by clicking on the moon and 
pointing to the tiles you want to switch.

This is a brick tile. It can't be cleared, 
but it can be moved. Eject it from the 
bottom of the playing field.

This tile is frozen. You can't move it 
until you melt it by placing two 
matching tiles next to it.

The magic pot is ready! Click it to use 
its power.

Instead of finding a dark and 
gloomy cave, he beheld a 
spacious gallery capped by a 
golden horn.

All the doors of the long street 
were marked with the same 
sign.

Forty thieves were hidden in the 
large urns.

The bouquet of white roses 
witnessed a wedding.

A strange figure slowly emerged 
from the lamp…

The ornate dishes were covered 
with equally lavish food.
Gems glinted on the golden plates.

The magic carpet couldn't 
wait to fly!

The fisherman peered at the 
brass flask with intense 
curiosity.

The four colored fish were used 
to pay tribute to the king.

The young king looked painfully 
at his stone legs.

Thanks to this bowl of water, the 
spell was broken and the young 
king came back to life.

Zumurrud quietly gave Ali 
Shar the bag of gold coins.
Life was hard, but satisfying.
Queen Zumurrud, 712 BC

When Ali Shar put down the 
sweet rice, he found Zumurrud 
standing before him.

The cask saved Sinbad the 
Seaman.

The roc flew with such speed 
that Sinbad was seized with 
giddiness.

They came upon a land of 
pumpkins.

A cherubic boy gifted the gold 
cane to Sinbad.

Hasan drank from the flagon of 
wine amid cheers.

A beautiful maiden brought 
Hasan a pair of gold-gilded 
slippers.

Hasan struck his old mother 
with a pine branch.

Hasan married the maiden 
that the empress loved most.
